frequency_question: How often do federal reviews of major institutional or professional accrediting agencies result in formal revocation of recognition within a specified two-year monitoring window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal proceeding by the U.S. Department of Education (or predecessor oversight bodies) to review, suspend, or revoke the recognition of a primary institutional or professional accrediting agency.

cases.name: American Bar Association (prior departmental reviews/threats of withdrawal)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) - 2016 initial withdrawal

provenance_note: claims 180 cases from only 4 named (45.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 4 major historical reference points detailed; broader universe of departmental recognition reviews totals approximately 180 distinct agency review cycles over three decades.
known_gaps: Lower-level compliance warnings and corrective action plans that did not proceed to formal termination proceedings are excluded from the hit numerator but included in the denominator.
skeleton: Federal oversight cycles of recognized accrediting agencies over a 30-year span, approximately 60 major agency reviews per decade, yielding roughly 180 total review cycles, with 2 final revocations fully executed.
validity_reason: Statutory framework governing federal recognition of accrediting agencies (Higher Education Act) remains stable across multiple congressional and administrative cycles.
